key_insight: Phosphoric acid-mediated molecular-scale welding locks carbon nanotubes into reorganized cellulose yarns, creating durable conductive textiles at low CNT loading.
engineering_relevance: The continuous process offers a route to robust all-textile sensors for wearable monitoring and human–machine interfaces.
method: Partially dissolve cellulose chains using phosphoric acid.
Regenerate cellulose in situ to lock CNTs within the reorganized yarn structure.
Integrate welded yarns into textiles for deformation, physiological, humidity, and volatile-organic sensing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports conductivity of 334.6 S m⁻¹ at 11.2 wt% CNT loading, improved mechanical tenacity and laundry durability over conventional coated fibers, and demonstrations of respiratory tracking and hand-gesture recognition.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify wash-cycle endurance or production-scale consistency, leaving long-term durability and manufacturing reproducibility to be verified.
paper_title: Continuous Molecular-Scale Welding of Carbon Nanotubes into Cellulose Yarns for Robust, Multisensory All-Textile Electronics
